title: Convergent Evolution: Why Does Nature Keep Reinventing the Same Solutions?
question: Why do unrelated species, separated by hundreds of millions of years and entire continents, independently evolve nearly identical solutions to the same problems?
summary: Camera eyes, wings, and streamlined bodies have each evolved independently many times over. Convergent evolution suggests the space of workable biological designs is far smaller than the space of imaginable organisms — evolution is a search process funneled by hard constraints, not a free wanderer.
